S28.01.note: Edit source only appears on the latest version and not for PDF, DOCX or image artifacts; the Save text is hidden on a narrow panel, so use its icon (title Save as a new version).
steps: Start a chat and ask for a short code file, for example a Python script, so a code artifact opens in the side panel.
Click the Source tab (icon with title Source) in the artifact header.
Click More artifact actions, then Edit source.
Change a line in the code editor, then click Save (title Save as a new version).
Compare: the edited code stays, and the version counter shows a new version (for example v2/2).
S28.01.where: Artifact panel > Source (tab) > More artifact actions > Edit source

S28.10.note: Without NEXT_PUBLIC_SANDBOX_ORIGIN the code uses a fallback frame where scripts may not run (apps/web/features/chat/components/SandboxedIframe.tsx:336-347), so the live result depends on the build; the plan says the sandbox switch-on is unfinished.
steps: Sign in and start a new chat.
Ask for a single-page web page in HTML, such as a page with a button and a text box.
Open the artifact from the chat so it shows in the side panel.
Make sure the Preview (eye icon) is selected in the artifact header.
Click the button or type in the text box on the page; compare: the page is live and responds.
S28.10.where: Chat > open an HTML artifact in the side panel > Preview (eye icon)

S28.11.note: Same sandbox dependency as S28.10: without NEXT_PUBLIC_SANDBOX_ORIGIN the fallback frame may not run React scripts (apps/web/features/chat/components/SandboxedIframe.tsx:336-347).
steps: Sign in and start a new chat.
Ask for a React component, such as a counter with two buttons.
Open the artifact in the side panel and make sure Preview (eye icon) is selected.
Click the buttons; compare: the component renders live and its state changes.
S28.11.where: Chat > open a React artifact in the side panel > Preview (eye icon)

S28.16.note: The Expected says overlay; the code replaces the preview area with a message panel (data-testid artifact-render-error) and also writes the error into the frame (infrastructure/sandbox/index.html:374-380). The message text is written with an HTML entity for the apostrophe.
steps: Ask for an HTML page whose script calls a function that does not exist as soon as it loads.
Open the artifact in the side panel with Preview selected.
Look for the message This artifact couldn't be rendered. with a detail line under it.
Click Retry to reload, or View source to open the code; compare: a way to recover is shown.
S28.16.where: Chat > open an HTML artifact that throws an error > Preview > error message in the panel

S28.18.note: The same action is also an icon button with aria-label Refresh preview in a different header layout.
steps: Open an HTML or React artifact in the side panel with Preview selected.
Click More artifact actions.
Click Refresh preview.
Compare: the preview reloads and shows the same content again, with any error message cleared.
S28.18.where: Artifact panel > More artifact actions > Refresh preview

S28.19.note: No control named Restart or a restart of the runtime was found. I searched Restart and restart in apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts, apps/web/app/chat/live-artifacts and apps/desktop/src. Closest are Refresh preview (ArtifactPreview.tsx, which only bumps a refresh key) and Refresh data (apps/web/app/chat/live-artifacts/LiveArtifactControls.tsx, which reloads connected-app data, not the runtime).

S28.24.note: The menu item text is built as Download source followed by the file extension in brackets; the button opens a menu only when the artifact has more than one download option.
steps: Open a code artifact, such as a Python script, in the side panel.
Click the Download artifact button (download icon) in the header.
If a menu opens, click Download source (.<extension>), where the extension matches the artifact language.
Open the saved file and compare: it holds the same code as the artifact.
S28.24.where: Artifact panel > Download artifact (button) > Download source (.<language>)

S28.25.needs: two or more artifacts in one account
S28.25.note: The button shows only when there are more than one artifacts, and the zip holds every artifact as a flat set (apps/web/features/chat/utils/downloadArtifacts.ts:157-162), not a project tree; the first step to open the panel was taken from the code's button title, not checked on screen.
steps: Create at least two artifacts in a chat, such as a code file and an HTML page.
Click the Artifacts button to open the artifacts panel.
Click Download all (title Download all artifacts as zip).
Open the downloaded artifacts.zip and compare: it contains the artifacts from the panel.
S28.25.where: Chat > Artifacts (button, title Artifacts) > Download all

S28.27.needs: a signed-in account; a private window for the last step
S28.27.note: The dialog and audience option text were found in the file, but I did not confirm the exact order of the dialog and the toast.
steps: Open a finished HTML or document artifact in the side panel.
Click Publish (on a narrow panel use More artifact actions, then Publish).
If a dialog asks about sharing, read it and confirm; the audience choice includes Anyone with the link.
Look for the message Published · link copied to clipboard, then open the link in a private window.
Compare: the shared artifact opens without signing in.
S28.27.where: Artifact panel > Publish (button) or More artifact actions > Publish

S28.30.needs: an artifact with two or more versions
S28.30.note: Restore adds the old version as a new latest version; Undo and Redo in More artifact actions also step between edits.
steps: Open an artifact that has at least two versions, for example after one Save in Edit source.
Click the version counter button (title Version history).
In the version list, click Restore on an earlier version.
Click Restore in the confirmation dialog titled Restore version N?.
Compare: the content goes back to the earlier version and the counter shows one more version.
S28.30.where: Artifact panel > Version history (version counter, for example v2/2) > Restore
